title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Quick follow-up on last week's reliability incident: we saw a short 5xx spike during morning peak that correlated with a thundering-herd of cache misses plus an autoscaler lag. Team reviewed retry policies, rate-limit backoffs, and possible Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. Agreed next steps include log dump, targeted benchmark from Redwood, and a small canary of increased min-replicas for 48h.
action_items: Ethan Ross: provide kube ingress + load balancer logs for 2026-05-21 incident (due: 2026-05-25)
Liam Chen: run focused benchmark reproducing 5xx pattern and share CSV (due: 2026-05-26)
Priya Nair: share sample requests and token distributions for peak window (due: 2026-05-24)
Maya Patel: send pricing delta for Dedicated min-capacity trial and security docs link (due: 2026-05-24)
next_steps: Redwood to run 3 targeted benchmarks simulating 10-20% higher QPS with cold-cache scenarios
Customer to provide logs and sample payloads for 05-21 08:30-09:15 PDT
Schedule 30-min canary kickoff once benchmark results available

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-23
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Wu (Redwood CSM); Sara Gomez (Nexa PM), Ethan Ross (Nexa SRE), Priya Nair (Nexa ML)
---
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check-in, we had the postmortem doc go out, we wanted to walk through the follow-up items. Ethan, do you want to start with what you saw?
00:18 Ethan: Yeah thanks; so on 05-21 about 08:42 our monitoring alerted - we saw a spike of 5xxs from the inference endpoints, roughly 3 to 4 minutes of elevated 5xx rate. It lined up with higher QPS from a campaign kickoff. Fastly-ish CDN showed normal, but kube ingress was seeing a burst of TCP connections.
00:36 Priya: And on our side model latency jumped too, a lot of cache misses on prefix KV; we saw cold KV hits around the same window. Could be correlated with the spikes.
00:54 Liam: Right, what I saw in the Redwood runtime was a queue pile-up when multiple clients triggered cold-cache population; autoscaler then took about 45 seconds to spin additional replicas which left a gap.
01:10 Sara: That matches the user reports - some calls timed out in the web app and retried, which probably amplified load.
01:25 Maya: So a classic combo: cache miss + autoscaler lag + retry storm. We flagged two immediate mitigations: 1) increase min replicas during business hours, 2) tune client retry/backoff to avoid tight loops.
01:42 Ethan: Quick q - your default retry policy in the SDK is what again?
01:47 Liam: By default we have 3 retries with exponential backoff starting at 100ms, max 2s with jitter. But customers often build their own wrappers and set lower backoffs.
02:05 Sara: We do have a wrapper that retries at 200ms fixed which probably made it worse.
02:12 Jordan: Noted. Also, we saw some 5xx classifications that were 503 gateway errors versus 504 timeouts; Liam, can you explain root causes for both?
02:25 Liam: 503s were service-unavailable on the model worker - typically overloaded OOM or too many concurrent requests per GPU. 504s are upstream timeouts, often when the runtime is waiting on kernel execution; both spike when you overload a node.
02:40 Priya: Any quick wins to prevent overload besides Dedicated?
02:47 Liam: A couple: aggressive prefix caching for common prompts, tune batching thresholds (smaller max batch in high variance workloads), and request-level concurrency limits on your side (client token bucket). Also, we can enable earlier shedding for extremely long requests.
03:05 Ethan: We use a mix of short prompts and some long chains for summarization; token distribution attached is heavy tail.
03:13 Priya: I uploaded a sample of top 500 requests to the drive - should help tuning.
03:20 Maya: Great. For the immediate action we recommend a 48h canary: bump min replicas from 2 to 4 during 07:30-10:30 PDT for weekdays. That should give headroom while autoscaler acts.
03:35 Sara: Cost impact?
03:38 Maya: We'll send a delta estimate - rough math is a 30% increase during the window; I'll include dedicated trial pricing which actually may be cheaper per-unit if you want predictable throughput.
03:48 Ethan: Regarding rate limits, we hit a 429 cluster-level limit? The logs show some 429s before 5xxs.
03:55 Liam: 429s can be emitted by our rate limiter when client side bursts exceed configured QPS. We can raise soft limits for your test account temporarily while watching for downstream 5xx. But must be careful - raising limits without headroom will just move pressure to the model workers.
04:15 Priya: Is there a way to see per-token cost during the spike? The console shows aggregated tokens but not per-request breakdown.
04:24 Jordan: We can provide a CSV of token breakdown for the benchmark run; also we'll share a temporary dashboard link for deeper inspection.
04:33 Ethan: For reproduction - what benchmark should we run? We tried a locust script but it didn't show the same failure mode.
04:40 Liam: Repro should simulate: bursty ramp (50% spike over baseline in 30s), mixed token lengths with a heavy tail, and cold KV ratio of ~30%. We'll provide a benchmark harness config.
04:58 Maya: Ok action items - Ethan to send logs, Priya to confirm sample payloads, Redwood to run benchmarks.
05:08 Sara: Another question - SOC2 and audit logs we requested last week, any update?
05:13 Maya: Yes, Jordan uploaded the security pack link in the workspace (see note). For Dedicated or Private deployment we have additional KMS options.
05:23 Priya: If we did Dedicated trial, can we pin GPUs to reduce noisy neighbors?
05:29 Liam: Yes Dedicated gives isolation and you can request specific GPU classes; also autoscaling is more predictable with reserved capacity. But procurement lead time is higher.
05:40 Ethan: For the short term we prefer to stay hosted and tune. If spikes persist, we'd evaluate Dedicated.
05:47 Jordan: Agreed. Also suggestion - enable a short-term client side token-bucket limiter with a burst size tuned to your peak, that helped other customers.
06:00 Sara: Sounds good. Can we get the benchmarks by next Tuesday?
06:05 Liam: We'll try to run them by Monday EOD and share results.
06:11 Priya: Also noticed a few transcription typos in the postmortem - not relevant but noted.
06:19 Maya: haha okay noted. Let's go through the log artifacts you mentioned. Ethan, anything specific in the ingress logs?
06:27 Ethan: We saw a slew of connections from same /user endpoint, many of which had identical prompt prefixes. That suggests caching could be effective. But at the time, the KV backend had evicted entries due to memory pressure.
06:43 Liam: Do you currently persist KV across restarts? If not, warm-up is required after autoscaler events.
06:49 Priya: We rely on in-memory KV - we can look at persisting popular prefixes to Redis fronting the runtime.
06:57 Liam: That could help but adds network latency; tradeoff to measure.
07:03 Sara: Any changes to our retry library you recommend immediately?
07:07 Liam: Increase exponential base to 300ms, add jitter +/-50%, and cap retries to 2 for POST generation endpoints. Avoid fixed 200ms retries.
07:18 Ethan: We'll push a config change to the wrapper and monitor.
07:22 Maya: Cool. On monitoring, we suggest an alert for queue length and a composite alert that triggers before 5xx rising.
07:30 Jordan: We'll include example alert rules in the doc.
07:36 Sara: Ok next - can Redwood share the benchmark job and the CSV?
07:40 Liam: Yes, I'll upload the harness and the result CSVs to the shared drive. Look for a file named "nexa_peak_benchmark_20260523.csv".
07:50 Priya: Regarding rate limiting, do you have per-route limits? We have some high-traffic inference routes and some low-traffic ones.
07:58 Liam: Yes per-route and per-api-key limits; we can set stricter limits on low-priority routes to protect high-priority ones.
08:06 Ethan: If we increase min replicas for 48h, we should monitor for any degradation in latency e2e.
08:12 Maya: We'll include latency histograms in the benchmark report.
08:17 Sara: Any concerns about data residency or logs if we enable Dedicated?
08:21 Maya: For Dedicated we can place instances in your region and flags for log retention. Also we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments.
08:30 Ethan: Ok. Are there any suggested rollback plans if the canary causes regressions?
08:34 Liam: Rollback is simply revert min-replicas and scale down; we also have automatic fallback policies to route to a lower-capacity model variant if latency or 5xx rises.
08:46 Priya: That fallback sounds useful - can we test it in staging?
08:50 Liam: Absolutely; we recommend a staged canary with traffic split 95/5 then ramp.
08:56 Maya: Recap - Ethan provides logs (due 05-25), Priya provides payloads (due 05-24), Redwood runs benchmarks (by 05-26), Maya sends pricing and security links (by 05-24). We will reconvene after benchmark.
09:12 Sara: One last thing - we saw occasional 502s mention of "redwood ded-uh-cate" in the postmortem, just typo?
09:18 Maya: Yeah that's the auto transcript; should read "Redwood Dedicated".
09:22 Ethan: ok thanks.
09:25 Maya: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email and upload artifacts.
09:29 Jordan: Thanks, bye.
09:31 Sara: Thanks, bye.
